brief: Open the diorama at 22.00 and nothing is happening anywhere. Every one of the ten itinerary branches in spawnLaneAgent opens with `sun &&` (`sun = daylight > 0.3`), so after dark every walker falls through to the final else and crosses the frame without stopping; kioskOpen, marketOpen, the band and eastOpen all close on the sun too. Night is ~40% of the clock, so two of every five viewers meet this town as a transit corridor with lit windows over it. Give it an evening: ONE place that keeps hours after dark, and people who go there and come back. Measure the dark first — on HEAD, count agents carrying a `stop` between 21.00 and 04.00 and print the number, because a clean zero is what makes the after worth reading.
successLooksLike: At a pinned 22.00 people are stopped somewhere, not only crossing, in both midsummer and midwinter. Over a folded night the count of agents with a `stop` rises off zero after dusk and returns to zero before dawn, with the margin printed. The DAY is untouched: noon population and the mix of kinds match a stashed HEAD baseline.
avoid: Do not widen `sun`. Night is not a dimmer day — the market and the allotments are shut for good reasons and reopening them is the cheap version of this brief. Build one evening place with its own hours and its own branch, and let the rest stay closed. Two laws bind hard: an event people must WALK to is bounded at both ends by things that are not the event (#32 — eastOpen closes the far bank at daylight 0.16, so anything east runs on a shorter clock than you think), and trip length sets standing population while the cap only sets inflow, so a 40 s evening round trip leaves its walkers on screen at 03.00. Check laneCap before adding an arrival source, and remember POP_FLOOR/scarcity already lifts arrival rates when the town is thin — measure with that in mind or you will credit yourself with its people.
